comparator.academicYear: Current UvA published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. The ACVA A–D skills line is published without separate EC and is integrated into the credited curriculum. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine free-choice/minor space, followed by diagnostics, professional skills, psychotherapy perspectives and a 15-EC empirical thesis. No specific minor or elective is invented.

questionsApplications.label: How do family, peers, school and society shape child and adolescent development?
How can developmental difficulties be assessed and young people and families be supported responsibly?
How can research evaluate developmental, educational and youth-support interventions?

alternatives.concept: Combines developmental and social psychology, cognition, family and peer contexts, sociology, communication, ethics and empirical methods to study children and adolescents in the environments where they grow up. It is the closest feasible UCR response, while UCR lacks dedicated pedagogy, family-support practice, diagnostics and supervised clinical training.

alternatives.concept: Develops the programme’s complex-development and youth-support strand through developmental psychology, psychopathology, psychodiagnostics, health psychology, neuroscience, biology, resilience and research methods. It does not claim to reproduce UvA clinical qualification or supervised practice.

alternatives.labelRationale: The curriculum gives sustained weight to developmental risk, mental health, assessment, biological context and evidence-based support.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Relative to the closest plan, this route replaces much of the sociology, communication and philosophy strand with biomedical foundations, public health, life science, ecology and advanced clinical-developmental psychology. Eleven courses differ, so the educational choice is substantially more health- and intervention-oriented.

alternatives.concept: Uses the programme’s family, social-environment, ethics, rights and policy evidence to organise sociology, political institutions, law, economic policy, gender history, inclusion and youth resilience around how society supports children and families.

It differs from both earlier plans by well over 30 EC and treats child development principally through rights, institutions and social conditions.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The family–school–society plan is the closest feasible UCR response. The official complex-development/youth-support and family/social-context evidence also supports distinct health/clinical and rights/policy directions. All three are coherent, feasible and pairwise differ by more than 30 EC, so production stops at three.

notes.text: The UvA programme is a dedicated Pedagogical Sciences degree with compulsory family pedagogy, school learning, professional child-support practice, diagnostics, a bachelor internship and an empirical thesis. UCR can build strong developmental, psychological, social, ethical, policy and research foundations, but it does not reproduce the profession-specific pedagogical and supervised clinical-skills sequence.
